args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, it failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The release candidate v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled back all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback the service is healthy, with an error rate of about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and check why it was promoted even though staging was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, it's healthy again, and I opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** I rolled all three regions back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.0 had been healthy there before, so no change-manager approval was needed. Afterward the service is healthy and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2) for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the result. It also lists two next steps: find out why v2.3.1 failed, and why it went to production even though its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
